critical_code_review_comments: next-no preview is non-atomic: counter is read but not consumed at preview time. Two simultaneous Save clicks could theoretically both see preview RN/26-27/003 but the actual POST uses atomic find_one_and_update so the persisted rn_no is guaranteed-unique. UI may briefly show a 'wrong' preview if two users save concurrently — acceptable.

POST /api/receipt-notes consumes the FY counter even on validation failure paths AFTER the increment? Verified ordering: validation runs BEFORE find_one_and_update, so failed creates do NOT burn a serial. Good.

ReceiptNoteCreate.invoice_date is a free string in payload (not date-validated); browser <input type='date'> ensures format but backend accepts any string including ''. Consider Pydantic date validation or empty-string normalization on backend if integrity matters.
Frontend lookupMakes triggers on EVERY blur even when part_no unchanged — minor extra request, not a bug.

MakeDropdown re-uses the literal value '__create__' as a SelectItem value; safe because radix Select treats it as a normal string but the option appears in a11y tree as '__create__' value with label '+ Create New Master' — acceptable.

StockInPage.jsx is 562 lines — close to the 700 line guideline but contains 5 well-separated components (StockInPage, ReceiptNoteTab, ReceiptNoteList, ReceiptNoteCreate, MakeDropdown, CreateMasterDialog, Detail, Field). Splitting into separate files would improve maintainability but is not blocking.
Detail dialog displays new Date(rn.created_at).toLocaleString() — assumes created_at is a parseable timestamp; backend writes now_iso() so this works. No timezone display indicator shown.
Sidebar Stock-In path was tested working; route /stock-in exists.
All interactive elements carry data-testid as required.
